strategies.name: Sequential All-Reduce with Interleaved Scaling
strategies.desc: Perform 8 sequential all-reduce operations with local scaling/unscaling between each stage, exactly as the reference implementation. Total 8 all-reduce dispatches with full vector payload each time. Simplest structure but highest dispatch count; no fusion or overlap opportunities exploited.

strategies.name: Fused Scale-Reduce with Vectorized Buffers
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all scale factors and fuse scaling operations into vectorized tensor operations before each all-reduce, eliminating per-shard loops by using broadcasting and view reshaping. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead through vectorization, trading memory for fewer scalar operations.

strategies.name: Pipelined Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair, enabling pipeline parallelism where scaling operations on gathered chunks can overlap with subsequent reduce-scatter communication. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller per-dispatch payloads and potential for hiding local computation in communication gaps.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction
strategies.desc: Exploit multi-node topology by splitting each all-reduce into intra-node followed by inter-node collectives, performing scaling operations at the intermediate aggregation point. Doubles dispatch count to 16 (8 stages × 2 levels) but reduces per-dispatch payload on the inter-node network and enables node-local optimizations.

strategies.name: Batched Multi-Stage with Single Dispatch
strategies.desc:
Restructure computation to stack all 8 stages as separate dimension in a batched tensor, perform all scaling transformations locally as batch operations, then use a single large all-reduce on the entire batch followed by local extraction of final stage. 1 all-reduce dispatch with 8× payload but maximum fusion of local operations and minimal dispatch overhead.
